scope: Reviewed named written/reading units; only explicitly indexed reusableSegments also supply complete exact Japanese character sounds.

review.note: Independent AI linguistic and provenance reviews, not certification by a human lexicographer. Included units have explicit dictionary sound assignments or independently supported word-local correspondences. Some moderate-confidence units have one lexical source reviewed by multiple agents; reviewer independence is not source independence. Unresolved sound ownership and rendering-convention cases are withheld.
review.soundReuse: Each reusableSegments index identifies a separately reviewed complete Japanese character-sound allocation. Its exact sound may support other independently attested pairs, including phonetic ateji; it authorizes no new sound transformations. This permission applies only to the indexed segments, independently of the named-unit scope of the remaining evidence. Explicit local ownership still takes precedence. Raw foreign transcriptions and neighbor-dependent allocations remain under their existing context checks.

facts.reason: The pinned 猿 page explicitly allocates the spider noun as 蜘ぐ/蛛も in 猿蜘蛛. JMdict 平たい/ひらたい independently fixes the omitted-okurigana stem 平ひらた. These three supported components exhaust this attested compound.
The pinned 狐 page explicitly assigns 遍べ and 羅ら in 狐遍羅. Both components recur unchanged in the attested fish noun.
The pinned 蛍 page explicitly assigns 魚こ in 蛍雑魚; 雑 independently reads ざつ, whose regular gemination before こ gives ざっ. The pinned word page independently attests ざっこ.

Daijisen and Nikkoku explicitly divide the classical verb as うれ・ふ. The selected JMdict reading is うれう: 憂 supplies the supported stem うれ, while the final historical ふ corresponds locally to う. This is an explicit kana correspondence, not script normalization.
Nikkoku explicitly divides あい‐むか・う and gives historical あひむかふ. 相あい and 向むか therefore keep their documented stem allocation, with final historical ふ corresponding locally to う.

The pinned 乾 page explicitly allocates 乾かれ/飯いい. The pinned 乾飯 page independently displays 飯い in another reading of the same food noun. JMdict attests both かれい and かれいい for this spelling, supporting contraction within the 飯 component.
The pinned 飛竜 word table explicitly assigns ペー and ロン to the two characters for this borrowed boat name. The selected hiragana transcription preserves that documented allocation.
The pinned 押 page explicitly assigns 忍す in 押おっ/忍す. Its independent kun reading お-す supplies 押お in the attested short greeting おす; no leftover substring is promoted into a new character reading.
The pinned 火病る word table explicitly supplies 火ふぁ and 病びょ, followed by the written verb ending る. The clipped borrowed sound remains local to this verb.
The pinned 木履 word table assigns 木ぽっく/履り and explicitly attests the voiced bokkuri variant. The local initial voicing preserves the complete ぼっく component under 木.
The pinned 古事記 table explicitly supplies 古ふる, 事こと and 記ふみ; an optional voiced override does not erase the unvoiced component listed in the table and selected in JMdict.

The pinned 端折る table explicitly assigns 端はし and 折ょ. In the nominal spelling without written り, the continuative ending remains under 折, giving ょり. 尻しり is independently supported. The small-kana onset is directly documented, not residual inference.
The pinned 柑子 table explicitly displays 柑こう and 子じ. Ordinary 色いろ follows that documented noun unchanged.

The pinned 蜻蛉洲 table keeps the two-character dragonfly unit together before 洲しま. JMdict lists あきつしま and あきずしま for this spelling; the selected local voiced form therefore remains within 蜻蛉, before independent 洲しま.

The pinned French letter pages independently name T té, G gé and V vé; the TGV page gives tégévé. These match the three adapted Japanese letter sounds て/じぇ/ゔぇ in the selected JMdict reading, including fullwidth glyphs.
The pinned 数 page explicitly allocates 巨ごん and 頭どう in the cetacean name 数歯巨頭. Ordinary 夢ゆめ precedes the same documented noun components.
The pinned 草履 table explicitly overrides the first character to じょう and assigns 履り; its noun headword lists the selected じょうり form. This is direct local evidence for the palatalized reading.

The pinned word table and compound analysis separate the cold noun 風邪 from 薬ぐすり. JMdict attests the local かざぐすり variant and the equivalent one-character spelling 風薬; 風 has the independent compound form かざ-. The supported boundary remains after the complete cold noun.

The pinned 鹹豆漿 table explicitly supplies 鹹しぇん, 豆どう and 漿じゃん. Independently, pinned KANJIDIC2 lists 豆トウ, and the selected JMdict transcription has the unvoiced とう. Keeping the outer borrowed components unchanged is a local transcription inference supported by these two readings; it does not claim that the word table itself prints とう.

JMdict independently pairs 可笑しい with おかしい, identifying the native adjective stem 可笑おかし. The compound places independently supported 口くち before that complete stem; no individual reading is invented for 可 or 笑.
The pinned 融 character source lists ゆ; the 融通 word table explicitly assigns voiced 通ずう, independently repeated in 神通. The selected ゆずう therefore has complete support for both characters.
The pinned 朋友 word table explicitly assigns 朋ぽん and 友ゆう and gives the ポンユー pronunciation. The selected long-vowel notation leaves the full ゆー under 友.

The same JMdict entry explicitly pairs 次第々々 with 次第次第 and しだいしだい. Independent 次し/第だい readings therefore map both iterations in sequence, preserving the two-character repetition rather than treating each mark as repeating its immediate predecessor.

Daijisen explicitly divides おち‐こち and individually marks both 遠 and 近 as nonstandard character readings; Nikkoku independently prints the same component division. The two deictic components keep their complete sounds, rather than choosing 遠お and transferring its final ち to 近. This is a local documented reading, not a new global character rule.
